verdict.rationale: Vue's docs describe it as an incrementally adoptable ecosystem that scales from a library to a full-featured framework. Buildless CDN usage is documented for enhancing static HTML, and official Router and Pinia libraries support full applications. A community report independently confirms that Vue can be added minimally to existing templates and calls gradual adoption a real selling point. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party guidance on the migration path between those stages (e.g. mounting Vue on page sections, then moving to SFC/build-tool apps) beyond tagline-level claims.

support.subject: As a developer, I can incrementally adopt the framework, scaling from a small part of a page up to a full application

citations.quote: A rich, incrementally adoptable ecosystem that scales between a library and a full-featured framework.
This makes the setup a lot simpler, and is suitable for enhancing static HTML or integrating with a backend framework.
Gradual adoption is a real selling point.
Official Libraries: Vue Router, Pinia, Tooling Guide
